Commentary.Commentary: The star with the ball was definitely Mehidy Hasan, scalping 4-29 off his 10 overs. He started off with the new ball and kept a probing line that the Windies batsmen found hard to get away. The rest of the bowlers were in form too, none of them giving away runs at more than 5 per over. Mashrafe Mortaza will definitely be happy with the performance and will hope that the batsmen can come out and get to this below-par total without any difficulties. The chase should be an easy one considering the form of the home team, especially Tamim Iqbal and Shakib Al Hasan and Mushfiqur Rahim. The left-handed opener from Chittagong has looked in good form but just hasn't got a big innings, but tonight seems to be a good opportunity to do so. All in all, unless something miraculous occurs over the period of the second innings, we should be seeing the Bangladeshis get their hand on the trophy. Join us for the chase in some time.

Bangladesh would have definitely taken this at the start of the day. 198 on a good looking pitch to bat shouldn't be enough if the hosts bat sensibly during the chase. Good tight bowling from the hosts combined with poor rash batting by the visitors has caused this. The fact that no batsman got to 20 other than Hope tells us the story. Right from the beginning, the visitors have been kept on a tight leash and never looked like getting to a big total. Shai Hope was a silver lining in this dark cloud of the Windies innings, getting to another century, his second on the trot. 108 not out from 131 balls was the need of the hour. It has at least given his bowlers something to defend.
Yorker to end the innings, the left-hander digs it out towards mid-wicket and gets a single on the last ball. Just four runs off the final over. WINDIES FINISH ON 198/9!

Rahim takes a sharp catch to dismiss Rovman. An excellent spell from the offie, he's turned this game in his side's favour for now. He finishes with figures of 10-1-29-4.

Hope gets behind the line, closes the face and defends it down in front of square leg.
Fraction straight in line, on a length, worked away on the leg side for nothing.
On the shorter side, outside off, played to cover-point.
FOUR! Some width on offer and Hope punishes that. Back of a length outside off, Shai hammers it through point. The man in the deep runs to his right and dives, but can't stop it.
Slanting across from a good length, Hope taps it down in front of point. Dot ball.
Tossed up on off, Bravo blocks it well.
Darren Bravo walks in at no.3.

OUT! Hemraj departs! Bowls short on off, Hemraj looks to cut but could not connect cleanly and ends up slicing it towards backward point where Mohammad Mithun dives to his left and takes a good catch. His poor form in the series continues. Another failure for him. Windies lose their first wicket.
FOUR! Second boundary for Hemraj. Short and flat on off, Hemraj cuts it through point for a boundary.
Flighted delivery on leg, Hemraj looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Short on off, Hemraj cuts it to point.
Tossed up on off, Hemraj defends off the front foot.
Length delivery outside off, Hemraj cuts it towards third man for a single.
Good length delivery on off, Hemraj looks to defend but gets a bottom edge on that one. It was just close to the stumps.
Length delivery on middle, Hemraj flicks it to mid-wicket.
Length delivery outside off, Hope cuts it towards point for a single.
Full outside off, Hope drives it again to covers. He is not finding the gap.
Full outside off, Hope drives it to covers.
FOUR! Nicely timed. Finds the gap with ease. Tossed up outside off, Hemraj plants his front foot forward and drives it through the covers for a boundary.
Some drift in and it creates a bit of problem. Fullish on off, Hemraj comes forward to push it away but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Pushes this full ball a bit square towards cover-point.
Touch quicker through the air on this occasion, on off, it's forced from the crease to the cover fielder.
Slower through the air, close to off, Hemraj is half forward in defense.
Comes from around the wicket and floats it up outside off, Hemraj comes forward and leaves it alone.
Mehidy Hasan to bowl from the other end with the second new ball.
Length delivery on off, Hope plays it to point.
FOUR! First boundary of the innings. Length delivery outside off, Hope punches it through point for a boundary. Good shot from Shai Hope.
Good length delivery on off, Hope keeps it out.
Length delivery on leg, Hemraj looks to flick but gets hit on the pads. The batsmen take a single. The umpire signals a leg bye.
Good length delivery on middle, Hemraj defends off the back foot.
Good length delivery outside off, Hemraj offers no shot.

We are ready to begin. This is Sylhet's first ODI game, becoming the 200th venue to host ODIs. Mustafizur Rahman will take the new ball first up. Chandrapaul Hemraj and Shai Hope will open the innings. Here we go...

Rovman Powell says Fabian Allen comes in for Oshane Thomas. States that they must do better as a batting unit and somebody has to bat through as that wins you matches. Ends by saying they will give their best to win the series.

Mashrafe Mortaza says the dew is a big factor here and it gets better for batting later on. Mentions it looks to be on the slower side and hopefully they can get the job done. On this being his 200th game, Mortaza says he feels proud of the achievement. Adds that his spinners are doing well, despite there being a shortage of wickets for them. Informs there are two changes as Imrul Kayes and Rubel Hossain go out and Mohammad Saifuddin and Mohammad Mithun comes in.
TOSS - Bangladesh win the toss and elect to bowl first!

Pitch Report - Tino Mawoyo out in the middle says that's there's an interesting texture on the surface. Adds that there are quite a few cracks, but it won't affect things much as the roller has gone over it and it's a good batting surface. Informs that 9 times teams batting second here have won. Ends by saying that the dew could be a factor because of the vegetation around.

Hello and welcome for the series decider. The series is levelled 1-1 and anything can happen in this final game. The Tigers took the first game, courtesy a good all-round performance, but then the Windies came roaring back in the second via an excellent Shai Hope ton. Consistency is the main issue for these two sides. Whichever can manage to find some of it, that team will end up winning. Bangladesh have been guilty of losing wickets in clusters and their opening woes still haunt them. The visitors will want to focus on their bowling unit, as it seems to run out of steam after a good start. Maybe a change or two to be expected? We'll see. So far, the team chasing has won in this series, so the toss becomes crucial. It's a rather early-ish start, so the dew won't come into play. Let's see what happens.
